questions.q: own exam-style Section B on your enquiry: (a) State your enquiry question. (1) (b) Describe one qualitative method. (2) (c) Explain your sampling strategy. (3) (d) Explain one way you presented data and why. (3) (e) Explain one anomaly in your results. (3) (f) Evaluate the reliability of your conclusions. (8)
questions.a: Indicative points: focused question; field sketch or photos with how; stratified-systematic with reasons; graph choice justified; anomaly with cause; strengths, limits and judgement
questions.model: Teacher reads (a) aloud and shows a one-mark answer, then starts the timer.

questions.q: Self-mark with the mark scheme and write two targets.
Rewrite your weakest answer to full marks.
questions.a: An improved answer matching the mark scheme

questions.q: State one quantitative method you used. (1)
questions.a: Timing infiltration of 500 ml of water in a tin ring
questions.model: State means a short fact. One method, named clearly. Timing how long 500 ml took to infiltrate.

questions.q: Explain one risk and how you reduced it. (2)
questions.a: Sharp tin edges could cut; edges were taped and an adult handled the tin
